title: The source keeps one recovery schema and one recovery_svc login; Architecture v5 has 19 schemas and 19 logins
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx
description: Version 4 of the Security and Access Design names one recovery schema and one login, recovery_svc, which holds USAGE on schema recovery and SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views, and it isolates that login from temporal_svc. Architecture v5 slide 29 and the naming rules of Rules v1 R4 give 19 Recovery schemas rwb_<name> with one login each, grants on the own schema only, and schema recovery reduced to the 30 read-only v_ace_* views. The source has no wording for the 19 logins and no statement of which login may read the views.
evidence: v4 section 7 rows 'Database', 'Read-only ACE access', 'recovery_svc isolation'; v4 section 1 row 'ACE data access'; v4 section 9 row 'Information disclosure'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 ('19 RECOVERY SCHEMAS - ONE LOGIN EACH'; 'each service has one database login that owns its schema and has no grant on any other schema; only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views') and slide 41; Rules v1 R4; ADR-014.
proposed: Section 7 is written per service: one login rwb_<short with _> per service, grants on the own schema only, rwb_source_data the only holder of the view grant, and the recovery_svc row replaced by a service login isolation row. Version 5 states the change in the realignment table at the end of the document.

title: The authorise contract has no request or response shape in any source
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 names the operations of rwb-access: POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies. None of the four has a row in the Endpoints sheet of the Ownership Map (156 operations) and none appears in the API Specification path list, so the payloads, the error codes and the cache-refresh behaviour that the guard library of DP-08 needs are not specified anywhere. The design names the operations and leaves the shape to the contract story.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 ('using cached permission data from rwb-access'), slide 14 ('REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA); GET /me/permissions; GET /doa-limits; /masking-policies') and slide 41 (P4 row, first API path /authorise); Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet: the closest rows are GET /admin/roles, GET /admin/access-log, GET /me/session and POST /admin/break-glass-grants. Rules v1 DP-08: H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
proposed: The contract is written in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and its fake in RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, both wave 1 contract stories, before any service builds against it. Version 5 names the four operations, their owner (P4) and the guard library owner (platform) and records that the shapes are open.

title: Two sources disagree on who applies the mask: rwb-source-data or each service
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 4 section 5 makes the API mask the control and holds the masking profile as data per role and field. Architecture v5 slide 39 answers 'masking is applied by rwb-source-data', while slide 35 says 'masking rules (P4) enforced in each service', and slide 11 routes only rwb-source-data to the views. With 19 services the two statements describe different controls: masking once at P1 in the contract, or masking in every service at its own API. The source document does not settle it.
evidence: v4 section 5 rows 'Masking', 'National ID', 'Audit of reads'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 35 ('masking rules (P4) enforced in each service', 'personal data masked and encrypted') and slide 39 FAQ ('masking is applied by rwb-source-data'); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: masking_rule to P4.
proposed: Both controls are kept and written as defence in depth: rwb-source-data masks in the view and in its contract, and each service re-applies the masking_rule rows of rwb-access before the response leaves. The story RWB-P4-E1037-APP owns the profile; the P1 story owns the view mask.

title: The mapping of a service workload identity to the SY- roles is not specified
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 4 says the Temporal authorizer plugin maps the OIDC role claim and the client certificate to the Workbench role, and gives SY-CASEWF rights to start and signal case workflows on rwb-case and SY-RULES the right to read rule package versions. With one workload identity per service and one certificate set per namespace, the document does not say which identity holds SY-CASEWF (only rwb-case, or every service that starts a child workflow) or whether SY-RULES is one identity shared by the 19 embedded Drools runtimes or one per service.
evidence: v4 section 4.1 rows SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES; v4 section 7.1 row 'Authorizer plugin'; v4 section 7 row 'Managed identities'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 ('Namespace mTLS; worker identity per service'), slide 35 ('Temporal namespaces have their own certificates and codec keys'); Temporal and Drools design L2 and L4.
proposed: Version 5 reads SY-CASEWF as the identity of P3 rwb-case and lets a calling service start a child workflow only through the CaseWorkflow signal, so no other service needs SY-CASEWF; SY-RULES is read as one role held by each service identity inside its own runtime.

title: The access log is named as an rwb_access object but has no row in the Ownership Map
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 put the access log in schema rwb_access, and version 4 section 8 makes it an append-only record. The Tables sheet of the Ownership Map (93 tables) has no access_log row, so the table has no ownership row, no key and no retention class in the map that every story uses.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 ('DB writes schema rwb_access: Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log') and slide 41 (P4 row); Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet: role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit are present, access_log is not; API row GET /admin/access-log is owned by P4.
owner_role: P4 rwb-access with the ACE DBA
proposed: P4 rwb-access owns the access log, as the row GET /admin/access-log already implies; the table is added to the Ownership Map at the next revision, with its own DB story in RWB-SVC-P4.

title: The view conformance test of RWB-E1-069 is split across two services
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx
description: Version 4 gives one test, 'Read-only ACE grant', and one story, RWB-E1-069. The split plan gives the legacy story slices in P1 (RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-DB), P4 (RWB-P4-E1069-APP) and integration (RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG). The document does not say which slice holds the pipeline check that fails the build, nor whether the check runs in the pipeline of rwb-source-data alone or in all 19.
evidence: v4 section 7 row 'Grant check' and section 10 row 'Read-only ACE grant'; split_plan.json legacy RWB-E1-069 slices RWB-P1-E1069-APP, RWB-P4-E1069-APP, RWB-P1-E1069-DB, RWB-ITG-E1069-ITG; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29 ('a boundary test in every build fails on any cross-schema reference').
owner_role: P1 rwb-source-data with the ACE DBA
proposed: The view conformance test sits with the P1 slice, which is the only holder of the grant, and the P4 slice keeps the role and masking checks. Version 5 names RWB-E1-069 as the view test and the per-service boundary test as the cross-schema check.

title: Partner users moved to S9 rwb-partner, while the approving role owner stays in P4
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
description: Version 4 has the partner and agency manager request partner users and the role owner approve them, inside one Workbench role model. The Ownership Map ruling moves partner_user to S9 rwb-partner (ASM-A6-tables-6) and keeps the internal role model in P4 rwb-access. The document does not say whether the approval is an S9 administrator action, a P4 role grant or both, and no partner API for creating a partner user appears in the operation list.
evidence: v4 section 6 bullet 3; Ownership Map v1 Rulings sheet row partner_user (S9; 'P4 keeps the internal role model only'); ownership.json tables partner_user owner S9; Endpoints sheet: GET /partners is S9 and GET /admin/roles is P4.
proposed: The partner user is created and ended by the S9 rwb-partner administrator, and the roles it holds are P4 role rows granted by the P4 role owner; both actions are written to the access log.

title: The codec server and the per-namespace codec keys have no owner and no rotation rule
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Security and Access Design v4.docx; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Version 4 gives the codec server a managed identity and the Key Vault key reference, with one key, and leaves key rotation as 'keeps old histories decodable'. Architecture v5 holds the keys per namespace, and slide 35 gives every Temporal namespace its own certificates and codec keys. The document does not name the owner of the codec server or of the key rotation, and the ownership map has no row for either.
evidence: v4 section 5 row 'Workflow history', section 7 rows 'Codec server' and 'Temporal certificates', section 7.1 row 'Payload codec'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes and slide 35 ('Temporal namespaces have their own certificates and codec keys'); ownership.json: no codec server or key object.
proposed: The codec server and the keys are platform components of RWB-PLT-E2038, one key per namespace with the old key kept for decode; the rotation is run by the platform under the key policy of SCB IT security.
